summary: Ulrike Roesler, a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies, earned her PhD at the University of Münster. She taught at the universities of Freiburg and Marburg, and held posts at the University of Oxford and Wolfson College.

Uma Chakravarti is a historian and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Mount Carmel College, Banaras Hindu University, and under D. Devahuti at the University of Delhi. She served as an educator at Miranda House from 1966 to 1998.
Umakant Premanand Shah was an Indologist and historian. His career included serving at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda as deputy director in 1954 and as head of the Ramayana Project in 1965.

Unnikrishnan Payyappallimana studied at Ayurveda College, Coimbatore, and the University of Amsterdam. He held research and visiting faculty posts at the Foundation for the Revitalization of Local Health Traditions, Amala Institute of Medical Sciences, and the University of Toyama.

Unrai Wogihara was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Junjirō Takakusu and Ernst Leumann at the University of Strasbourg. He later held posts at the University of Tokyo, Taisho University, and Shiba Junior & Senior High School.
Unsho Shaku was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Mount Koya in 1844. He taught Ekai Kawaguchi and founded both the Kairitsu Gakko and the Juzenkai in 1884.

Uranchimeg Borjigd Ujeed is a scholar of Buddhist and Central Asian studies who earned her PhD from SOAS University of London. She has served as a Research Associate in the Mongolia and Inner Asia Unit at Cambridge.

Uranchimeg Tsultem is a scholar of Buddhist studies and art history who earned her PhD at UC Berkeley. She held posts at the Mongolian National University of Arts and Culture, National University of Mongolia, UC Berkeley, and IUPUI.

Urs App is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD at Temple University and studied under Yoshitaka Iriya and Seizan Yanagida. He held posts at Hanazono University and the International Research Institute for Zen Buddhism.
Usha Nilsson was an Indologist and linguist who served as a faculty member and Emeritus Professor of Languages and Cultures of Asia at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.
Uta Reinöhl is a linguist and Indologist who held a post at the University of Cologne in 2018 and serves as Chair of General Linguistics at the University of Freiburg.

Ute Hüsken is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her doctorate under Heinz Bechert at Göttingen. She taught at Göttingen and served as a professor at the University of Oslo and Heidelberg University.

Utz Podzeit was an Indologist who earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Vienna, where he was appointed Universitätsdozent in 1969. He also undertook a research stay at the University of Madras from 1972 to 1974.
V. Kameswari is an Indologist associated with the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, where she has served as an Editorial Committee member and research supervisor.
V. P. Bhatta is an Indologist and linguist who has served as head and Professor-Editor of the Sanskrit Dictionary Project at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.
V. R. Srinivasan is an Indology and history scholar who pursued PhD research at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under the doctoral supervision of V. Yamuna Devi.

V. Raghavan was an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Madras under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He taught Sanskrit at the University of Madras (1934–1968) and helped found and run the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute.
Vaibhav Singh is a scholar of Indology and history who earned his PhD from the University of Reading in 2017 and held a post there.
Valaiyattur Venkayya was an Indologist and historian who studied at Madras Christian College and the University of Madras, and later succeeded Eugen Hultzsch.

Valdo H. Viglielmo was a Japanologist and philosopher who earned his degrees at Harvard. After teaching at Harvard, Meiji Gakuin, International Christian University, and Princeton, he served as a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi from 1965 to 2002.
